fields.meta_title: Accounting Automation for the Month-End Close | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Accounting automation that reconciles your bank account each night and drafts recurring entries for approval, built around your ledger.
fields.h1: Build Accounting Automation for Your Month-End Close
fields.hero_description: Get accounting automation that matches bank lines overnight and holds recurring entries for the controller.
fields.features_heading: Where a Finance Team Loses Hours Each Month
fields.features_subheading: Accounting automation is software and AI taking over the manual steps of the books. Your team reviews exceptions, not every entry.
fields.feature_1:
Close rules you write as sentences

Describe each rule the way you would brief a new hire: match on amount and date. Emergent builds the app and its logic from those words, and you change a rule by prompting.
fields.feature_2:
A two-way link to your ledger

The app reads accounts and balances from QuickBooks or NetSuite through their APIs and writes approved entries back. Nobody retypes a number from one system into another.
fields.feature_3:
Receipts and bills read into fields

Upload a receipt or a vendor bill and AI reads the vendor, date, and amount into structured fields. A value it is unsure of goes to a person to confirm before it is used.
fields.feature_4:
Reminders that reach the task owner

Each close task has one owner and a due day. When a task slips, its owner hears about it in Slack or by email, and a task still open a day later goes to the controller.
fields.feature_5:
One live board for the whole close

Matched lines and entries awaiting approval update on one dashboard as they change. Every record sits in a database you own, ready when the auditors ask for last quarter.
fields.feature_6:
The code behind your close, exported

Paid plans export the full code of the app, matching rules included, to your GitHub repository. An engineer can read how a line was matched and review each change to it.

fields.tab_content_1:
Bank lines match overnight, and 7 go to a person

Every night the app pulls the bank lines from Quillmont Tile Supply's operating account and matches each one to a ledger entry by amount and date. Last night 405 of 412 lines matched. The 7 that did not went to Corinne Vasquez, the staff accountant, each beside the closest entry in the ledger.
fields.tab_content_2:
Day 3 of the close, and one accrual is late

Quillmont runs a 5-day close. On day 3 of the September close, the board shows 31 of 38 tasks done and 6 more on schedule. The freight accrual, owned by Teodor Lindqvist, was due on day 2. It turns red on the board, and Teodor gets a direct message with the task and its due day.
fields.tab_content_3:
Each $1,500 insurance entry waits for the controller

Quillmont paid $18,000 up front for a 12-month liability policy. On the last day of each month, the app drafts a $1,500 entry that moves one month of the policy from prepaid insurance to insurance expense. The draft waits for the controller, Augustin Mbatha. It posts to QuickBooks once he approves it.
fields.tab_content_4:
A $6,800 jump in software spend needs a note

Any account that moves more than 10% from the prior month needs a note from its owner. Software subscriptions rose $6,800, from $42,300 in August to $49,100 in September. Saoirse Kalani owns the account. The app asks her for the reason, and the account stays open on the close board until she writes it.

fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan accounting automation around your close calendar, then build and test it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Pick the step that eats the most hours
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Connect the ledger and the bank lines
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Write each rule as a sentence
fields.howto_step_1_des: List every task in last month's close with its owner and the hours it took. Sort the list by hours. The tasks at the top that follow a fixed rule, such as matching or a recurring entry, are where to start.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Choose one task to automate first, not the whole close. Bank matching makes a good first pick for a small team: the rule is plain, every line has an amount and a date, and a miss is easy to spot.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Connect your ledger through its API so the app can read accounts and write entries back. Bring in bank lines from your bank's export or a connected feed, and keep one record per line so each match can be traced.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Prompt the rules the way you would explain them to a new staff accountant: match on amount and date, allow a 2-day gap for card deposits, send anything else to a named person. Emergent turns those sentences into the app and its database.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Decide which entries post on their own and which wait for a person. Put the controller on anything that moves a balance by judgment, such as accruals and write-offs, and log every approval with a name and a time.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Run a closed month through it
fields.howto_step_6_des: Load last month's bank lines and entries, which your team has already closed by hand. Compare what the app matched and drafted with what your team booked, line by line. Fix a rule by prompting, then run the month again.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Run one close side by side
fields.howto_step_7_des: For the next close, let the app run next to your current process. Compare the two results at the end, then switch the manual task off. Add the next automation only after a clean close.

faq_plan.a: Automation in accounting is the use of software and AI tools to replace manual accounting tasks with automated workflows. In accounting automation, the rules do the repeatable work, and the accountant's job shifts from keying entries to checking what the rules could not settle.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up accounting automation?
faq_plan.a: Start with one task from your close, then describe it in Emergent's AI automation builder as plain rules: what to match, what to draft, and who approves. Emergent builds the app with its database and dashboard. Once you connect the app to your ledger, it reads the chart of accounts, and the rules run on your real accounts.

faq_plan.q: What is the best accounting automation tool?
faq_plan.ref: What is the best accounting automation tool?

prov.original: What is the best accounting automation tool?

faq_plan.a: The best accounting automation tool is the one that works with the ledger you already run and takes over your slowest close task. A team that loses two days to bank matching needs strong matching rules, while a team stuck waiting on sign-offs needs approvals and reminders. Shortlist on that fit before you compare feature lists.

faq_plan.q: What are some examples of accounting automation?
faq_plan.ref: What are some examples of accounting automation?

prov.original: What are some examples of accounting automation?

faq_plan.a: Examples include matching bank lines to the ledger, drafting recurring journal entries, tracking close tasks by owner, and asking for a note when a balance swings. Paying vendor bills is its own flow, covered under accounts payable automation.

faq_plan.q: What is the best accounting automation software?
faq_plan.ref: What is the best accounting automation software?

prov.original: What is the best accounting automation software?

faq_plan.a: No one product is the best accounting automation software for every team: the right one fits your ledger, your volume, and who has to approve what. Ask each vendor to run 30 days of your own bank lines before you sign. Emergent builds the software around your rules instead of a fixed template, and every record lands in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: What is automated accounting software used for?
faq_plan.a: Automated accounting software is used for the repeatable parts of the books, run on a schedule or a trigger. It matches bank lines to the ledger and drafts entries, then hands each exception to a person. It can live inside your ledger or run beside it and write approved results back.

faq_plan.q: What does accounting workflow automation include?
faq_plan.a: Accounting workflow automation includes the hand-offs between people as well as single tasks: who prepares an entry, who reviews it, and what happens when a step runs late. A reconciliation that a preparer signs and a reviewer signs off is one case. Monthly packs for management are a separate job, handled by report automation.

faq_plan.q: What is the top rated accounting automation software with integration?
faq_plan.ref: what's the top rated accounting automation software with integration
faq_plan.a: The top rated choice for your team is the software whose integrations reach your ledger and your bank without manual exports. Ask whether approved entries post back to the ledger on their own or wait in a file someone uploads. Apps built with Emergent connect to any tool that has an API and sync data in both directions.

faq_plan.q: How much does accounting automation software cost?
faq_plan.ref: how much does accounting automation software cost
faq_plan.a: The cost depends on the billing unit. Price accounting automation software on your own numbers: monthly bank lines and the number of entities and logins. Ask for the setup fee and the price at twice your current volume, because quarter-end runs heavier. Emergent is free to start, and the free tier covers building and publishing an app.

faq_plan.q: How to choose accounting automation software for medium-sized companies?
faq_plan.ref: how to choose accounting automation software for medium-sized companies
faq_plan.a: Choose software that handles more than one entity and lets you name an approver for each type of entry, since a medium-sized company splits the close across several people. Check that it writes back to your ledger and records who approved what. If customer bills are the bottleneck, start with invoice automation and add the close after.

plan.angle: The top 10 are vendor suites and glossaries that define accounting automation in general terms. This page shows four automations a small finance team builds around the ledger it already runs, drawn as working screens for one month-end close at Quillmont Tile Supply: 405 of 412 bank lines matched overnight with 7 sent to a staff accountant, a close board that flags a late freight accrual on day 3, a $1,500 monthly insurance entry held for the controller, and a 16% jump in software spend that needs the account owner's note before close. The FAQ answers the tool, cost and examples questions searchers compare.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build Accounting Automation for Your Month-End Close'; hero 'Get accounting automation that matches bank lines overnight and holds recurring entries for the controller.' frames the whole close, not one feature or a sibling (AP, invoice, bookkeeping).

intent.evidence: Top 10 (IBM, Zuora, BlackLine, Karbon, Numeric) define the term, list examples and compare software; the page defines it (section intro, FAQ 1 sourced to IBM), shows four worked close automations, answers the PAA examples/best-tool/best-software questions and cost, plus a seven-step how-to.

specificity.evidence: Finance-team vocabulary: 'prepaid insurance to insurance expense', 'freight accrual', '5-day close', 'staff accountant', 'more than 10% from the prior month needs a note'.

openers.evidence: Paragraphs open on full sentences: 'Every night the app pulls the bank lines...', 'Quillmont runs a 5-day close.', 'List every task in last month's close...'.

craft.evidence: QC Q2/Q5/Q7 clean; notes recorded for repeated ideas and the step 4 33-word sentence.

voice.evidence: Operator detail: 'Last night 405 of 412 lines matched', 'allow a 2-day gap for card deposits', 'Ask for the setup fee and the price at twice your current volume'.

truth.evidence: FAQ 2 states platform behaviour as automatic: 'Emergent builds the app with its database and dashboard, and reads your chart of accounts from the ledger before the first rule runs.' Numbers agree everywhere: 405 + 7 = 412; 31 + 6 + 1 = 38; $18,000 / 12 = $1,500; $49,100 - $42,300 = $6,800 (+16%, over the 10% rule); prepaid-to-expense direction correct; definition matches the IBM quote.

distinct.evidence: Close-centred stories (bank matching, close board, recurring prepaid entry, variance note) distinct from AP, invoice and bookkeeping siblings, which are linked rather than headlined.

faq.evidence: 10 items, definition first, hub link in item 2, sibling links (accounts payable automation, report automation, invoice automation). Notes on the duplicated 'best tool' / 'best software' answers.
